back: The sentence (usually first) that states the main idea of a paragraph; every other sentence supports it.
Every sentence in the paragraph is about the one idea in the topic sentence; no drifting sentences.
Writing flows logically so the reader can follow how ideas connect; created by connectives, pronouns and repeated key words.
Analyse the title, plan, write, check.
notes: Roughly 10% of the time planning, 75% writing, 15% checking.

front: Three questions to ask about a title
back: What type of writing is wanted? What exactly is the topic? Is there a limit (time, place, person, situation)?

front: When to start a new paragraph
back: For a new idea, a new time, a new place or a new speaker.
however, on the other hand, nevertheless, yet, in contrast
as a result, consequently, therefore, so, because of this
Close, not repeat: resolve the story, restate the position firmly, or give a reasoned judgement.
Start with a time phrase, an -ing phrase, a subordinate clause (Although…), or occasionally a single word; mix short and long sentences.
